evidence.quote: This uses the decomposition in rational Chow motives, not finite-dimensionality alone.

exclusions.query: Pure Tate consequences from finite-dimensionality alone
exclusions.reason: The conclusion requires the rational Tate decomposition.

hypotheses.statement: Let $S$ be a smooth connected projective surface over $\mathbb C$ with $p_g(S)=q(S)=0$.
Let $S$ be a smooth connected projective surface over $\mathbb C$ with $p_g(S)=0$.
Let $S$ be a smooth connected projective surface over $\mathbb C$ with $p_g(S)=0$.
Let $\pi:\widetilde X\to X$ be the blowup of a smooth projective surface at a point.
To prove Theorem 1 with rational coefficients, it is enough to prove it for smooth minimal surfaces $X_0$ of general type with $p_g=q=0$.
The fixed-target derived arrow stack has an open substack $\mathfrak U$ whose truncation $U$ is the ordinary Quot scheme with the chosen rank and Hilbert polynomial, before fixing determinant.
Let $\mathfrak Z$ be a locally geometric derived stack, locally of finite presentation, whose classical truncation $j:Z\to\mathfrak Z$ is a scheme.
Let $0\to F\to V_0\to Q_0\to0$ be an exact sequence on $X$, where $V_0$ is a vector bundle of rank $r$ and $Q_0$ is torsion.
The scheme $B$ has a $G$-equivariant closed embedding in a smooth projective scheme.
The enhancement $\mathfrak W$ induces a perfect obstruction theory $E_W\to L_W$.
Let $R$ be a noetherian parameter scheme and let $L_R\twoheadrightarrow Q$ be a flat family of rank-zero quotients of a line bundle on $X\times R$.
Suppose $g:Y\to Z$ is smooth and carries a relative perfect obstruction theory $E_g\to L_{Y/Z}$ of amplitude $[-1,0]$.
Assume $p_g=q=0$.

On the product $U_b=\mathop{\mathrm{Div}}^{D_b}(X)\times X^{[n_b]}$, the rank-one Quot virtual class is $$\label{fix:low-product}
 [U_b]^\mathrm{vir}=
 \mathop{\mathrm{e}}(F_b)\cap
       \bigl([\mathop{\mathrm{Div}}^{D_b}(X)]^\mathrm{vir}\times[X^{[n_b]}]\bigr).$$
In the auxiliary setting a divisor component with $m_P<0$ has zero virtual class.

For the divisor component whose Picard component contains $K$, there is an integer $s>0$ such that $$\label{eq:canonical-cycle}
 [\mathop{\mathrm{Div}}^{K}(X)]^\mathrm{vir}=-s[z].$$ Here $\mathop{\mathrm{Div}}^{K}(X)$ allows variation of the line in its Picard component; $z$ is the unique effective canonical divisor.
Assume $p_g=q=1$, $K$ ample, and $D=3K$.
Let $r>0$, and let $N_r=X^{[r-1,r]}$ be the scheme of nested subschemes $Z'\subset Z$ of lengths $r-1,r$.
Fix a finite list of line bundles on $X$.

The class in [rel:fiber-contribution] admits a decomposition $$C_*(T,H;n_1,n_2)=c_*[\Delta_X]+\Gamma_*, \qquad \Gamma_*\in\sum_{a+b=2}R_X^a\boxtimes R_X^b. \label{rel:universal-decomposition}$$ One can choose $c_*$ by a fixed universal rule.
For either surface setting, and any $p\geq0$ with $v>p+2$, sum the classes [rel:fiber-contribution] with the following multiplicities:* 1.
If $p_g=q=0$ and the coefficient $c$ in [rel:chow-identity] is nonzero, then $\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}_0(X)^0\otimes\mathbb Q=0$.
Suppose $1\leq k_0\leq8$.
If $\Lambda$ is odd, there is a line bundle $h_0$ on $X_0$ with $$h_0^2=-1,\qquad K_0h_0=1.$$ If $\Lambda$ is even, then $k_0=8$ and there is a line bundle $h_0$ with $$h_0^2=0,\qquad K_0h_0=2.$$
Let $P$ be an effective line bundle on $X$ such that $m_P\geq0$ and $\alpha P\ne0$.
The actual line bundles $$H=K+h',\qquad T=(d-1)K-h'$$ are effective and satisfy [nr:survivors], with $\alpha H\ne0$.
Let $X$ be a smooth minimal projective complex surface of general type with $p_g(X)=q(X)=0$ and $K_X^2=9$.
For the data [r1:data], with numerical inputs $K^2=9$ and $\int c_2=3$, the two-order middle coefficient is $$c_{\mathrm{mid}}=12.$$

evidence.quote: Vanishing after tensoring with $\mathbb Q$ means that some nonzero integer annihilates $z$.

outputs.exact_statement: Let $S$ be a smooth connected projective surface over $\mathbb C$ with $p_g(S)=q(S)=0$. Then $$\deg:\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}_0(S)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z$$ is an isomorphism, where $\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}_0(S)$ has integral coefficients.

Let $S$ be a smooth connected projective surface over $\mathbb C$ with $p_g(S)=0$. Then the Albanese homomorphism $$\operatorname{alb}_S:\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}_0(S)^0\longrightarrow\mathop{\mathrm{Alb}}(S)(\mathbb C)$$ is an isomorphism of abelian groups, where $\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}_0(S)$ has integral coefficients.

Let $S$ be a smooth connected projective surface over $\mathbb C$ with $p_g(S)=0$. Then $h(S)_{\mathbb Q}$ is finite-dimensional in the sense of Kimura and $t_2(S)=0$.*

*If, in addition, $q(S)=0$, then $$h(S)_{\mathbb Q}\simeq
\mathbf 1\oplus\mathbb L^{\oplus b_2(S)}\oplus\mathbb L^2.$$ In this case, for every $m,n\ge0$, the rational Chow motives of the power $S^m$ and the Hilbert scheme $S^{[n]}$ of length-$n$ zero-dimensional subschemes are pure Tate, with $S^0=S^{[0]}=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C$. For $Y=S^m$ or $Y=S^{[n]}$, the rational cycle-class maps satisfy $$\operatorname{cl}_Y^i:\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}^i(Y)_{\mathbb Q}
 \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}H^{2i}(Y,\mathbb Q),
\qquad H^{2i+1}(Y,\mathbb Q)=0
\quad\text{for every }i\ge0.$$

Let $\pi:\widetilde X\to X$ be the blowup of a smooth projective surface at a point. Then $p_g$ and $q$ are unchanged, and $$\pi_*:\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}_0(\widetilde X)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}_0(X)$$ is a degree-preserving isomorphism with integral coefficients. Consequently these assertions are invariant under birational maps between smooth projective surfaces.

To prove Theorem 1 with rational coefficients, it is enough to prove it for smooth minimal surfaces $X_0$ of general type with $p_g=q=0$. For such a surface, putting $k_0=K_{X_0}^2$, one has $$\label{eq:reduction-invariants} 1\le k_0\le9,\qquad \chi(\mathcal O_{X_0})=1,\qquad \int_{X_0}c_2(X_0)=12-k_0,\qquad b_2(X_0)=10-k_0.$$ It is also enough to prove the assertion on any chosen sequence of point blowups of each such $X_0$.

Let $\mathfrak Z$ be a locally geometric derived stack, locally of finite presentation, whose classical truncation $j:Z\to\mathfrak Z$ is a scheme. Suppose $E_Z=j^*L_{\mathfrak Z}$ is perfect of Tor-amplitude $[-1,0]$. The canonical map $$\phi_Z:E_Z\longrightarrow L_Z$$ has cone in $D^{\leq-2}(Z)$, and is a perfect obstruction theory. For a map of such enhancements, the induced cotangent map commutes with the corresponding maps $\phi_Z$.

Let $0\to F\to V_0\to Q_0\to0$ be an exact sequence on $X$, where $V_0$ is a vector bundle of rank $r$ and $Q_0$ is torsion. The map $$\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}^1(F,Q_0)\longrightarrow\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}^2(F,F)
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{tr}}H^2(\mathcal O_X)$$ is surjective if $p_g=0$. It is also surjective if $K$ is ample and $Kc_1(Q_0)>rK^2$.

The scheme $B$ has a $G$-equivariant closed embedding in a smooth projective scheme. Its obstruction theory has a global presentation by two $G$-equivariant vector bundles. The morphism to the truncated cotangent complex can be represented by a morphism of two-term complexes for this embedding.

Suppose $g:Y\to Z$ is smooth and carries a relative perfect obstruction theory $E_g\to L_{Y/Z}$ of amplitude $[-1,0]$. Then $\mathop{\mathrm{Ob}}_g=h^1(E_g^\vee)$ is a vector bundle, $$[\mathop{\mathrm{Ob}}_g]=[T_{Y/Z}]-[E_g^\vee]\quad\hbox{in }K^0(Y),$$ and its virtual pullback is $$\label{fix:smooth-operation}
 g^!\gamma=\mathop{\mathrm{e}}(\mathop{\mathrm{Ob}}_g)\cap g^*\gamma.$$ The formula holds over arbitrary base cycles. For $Z$ a point, it says $[Y]^\mathrm{vir}=\mathop{\mathrm{e}}(\mathop{\mathrm{Ob}}_Y)\cap[Y]$.

Assume $p_g=q=0$. A nonempty fixed part with lines $T,H$ and lengths satisfying [eq:length] is the smooth product $$W=|T|\times|H|\times X^{[n_1]}\times X^{[n_2]}.$$ Let $x_i=c_1(\mathcal O_{|D_i|}(1))$, with $D_1=T,D_2=H$. The fixed virtual class is $$\label{fix:pg0-class} [W]^\mathrm{vir}= \prod_{i=1}^2\bigl(x_i^{h^1(D_i)}\mathop{\mathrm{e}}(F_i)\bigr)\cap[W], \qquad F_i=\bigl((K-D_i)^{[n_i]}\bigr)^\vee\otimes\mathcal O(1_i).$$ A part with either $m_T<0$ or $m_H<0$ contributes zero. For the other parts, after including $\mathop{\mathrm{e}}(F_1)\mathop{\mathrm{e}}(F_2)$, pushforward over the linear systems is coefficient extraction at $[x_1^{m_T}x_2^{m_H}]$.

On the product $U_b=\mathop{\mathrm{Div}}^{D_b}(X)\times X^{[n_b]}$, the rank-one Quot virtual class is $$\label{fix:low-product}
 [U_b]^\mathrm{vir}=
 \mathop{\mathrm{e}}(F_b)\cap
       \bigl([\mathop{\mathrm{Div}}^{D_b}(X)]^\mathrm{vir}\times[X^{[n_b]}]\bigr).$$

In the auxiliary setting a divisor component with $m_P<0$ has zero virtual class. If $m_P\ge0$, its virtual class is supported, by cosection localization, on the empty divisor or on the unique canonical divisor $z$. The empty-divisor class is the reduced point with coefficient one. Only the Picard component containing $K$ can give the canonical contribution.

For the divisor component whose Picard component contains $K$, there is an integer $s>0$ such that $$\label{eq:canonical-cycle}
 [\mathop{\mathrm{Div}}^{K}(X)]^\mathrm{vir}=-s[z].$$ Here $\mathop{\mathrm{Div}}^{K}(X)$ allows variation of the line in its Picard component; $z$ is the unique effective canonical divisor.

Assume $p_g=q=1$, $K$ ample, and $D=3K$. Every fixed contribution vanishes except those obtained from a low divisor equal to the empty divisor or to the canonical divisor. In either surviving case the contribution is computed on the actual fiber $$|D_a|\times X^{[n_a]}\times X^{[n_b]},$$ with the factors $\mathop{\mathrm{e}}(F_a)\mathop{\mathrm{e}}(F_b)$. The low hyperplane is $x_b=0$ and $m_{D_b}=0$; pushforward over $|D_a|$ is extraction at $x_a^{m_{D_a}}$. The overall multiplier is $1$ for the empty divisor and $-s$, with the same $s>0$ as in [eq:canonical-cycle], for the canonical divisor. The statement applies to operational insertions in universal perfect complexes, also after adjoining marked surface factors.

Let $r>0$, and let $N_r=X^{[r-1,r]}$ be the scheme of nested subschemes $Z'\subset Z$ of lengths $r-1,r$. Write $$\psi:N_r\longrightarrow X^{[r]},\quad
 \phi:N_r\longrightarrow X^{[r-1]},\quad
 \rho:N_r\longrightarrow X$$ for the two forgetful maps and the residual-point map. Then $N_r$ is smooth, projective, irreducible of dimension $2r$; $\psi_*[N_r]=r[X^{[r]}]$; and, with quotient-line convention, $$\sigma=(\phi,\rho):N_r
 =\mathbb P(\mathcal I_{r-1})
 \longrightarrow X^{[r-1]}\times X.$$ Put $\mathcal L=\mathcal O_{N_r}(1)$ and $\zeta=c_1(\mathcal L)$. If $j:N_r%
  %
  \mathrel{%
    \BeginAccSupp{method=hex,unicode,space=false,pdfliteral=direct,ActualText=21AA}%
    \lhook\joinrel\rightarrow%
    \EndAccSupp{pdfliteral=direct}%
  }%
%
N_r\times X$ is the graph of $\rho$, then $$0\longrightarrow(\psi\times\mathop{\mathrm{id}}_X)^*\mathcal I_r
 \longrightarrow(\phi\times\mathop{\mathrm{id}}_X)^*\mathcal I_{r-1}
 \longrightarrow j_*\mathcal L\longrightarrow0.
 \label{rel:universal-ideal-sequence}$$ For a two-term vector bundle resolution $0\to U_1\to U_0\to\mathcal I_{r-1}\to0$ on $X^{[r-1]}\times X$, one has, for every $k\geq0$, $$\sigma_*(\zeta^k\cap[N_r])
 =\left[\frac{c(U_1^\vee)}{c(U_0^\vee)}\right]_k
 \cap[X^{[r-1]}\times X].
 \label{rel:projective-pushdown}$$ All these identities remain valid after adjoining other Hilbert or surface factors.

Fix a finite list of line bundles on $X$. Consider a finite polynomial of Chern characters of universal point ideals and their derived duals, together with Chern classes of these lines and of $T_X$ pulled from the surface slots and equality diagonals between those slots, on $$X^{[n_1]}\times X^{[n_2]}\times X^\ell,
 \qquad \ell\geq2.$$ Keep two specified surface factors as outputs and push forward over the Hilbert factors and all other surface factors. The resulting Chow class is a finite rational linear combination of pushforwards of products of equality diagonals and line and tangent classes on powers of $X$. The coefficients and the list of such products can be chosen by one recursion independent of $X$ and of the chosen line bundles.

The class in [rel:fiber-contribution] admits a decomposition $$C_*(T,H;n_1,n_2)=c_*[\Delta_X]+\Gamma_*, \qquad \Gamma_*\in\sum_{a+b=2}R_X^a\boxtimes R_X^b. \label{rel:universal-decomposition}$$ One can choose $c_*$ by a fixed universal rule. Besides the integer parameters and the chosen weights, this rule depends only on $$\int_X c_2(T_X),\qquad \int_X UV\quad (U,V\in\{K,L_1,L_2,T,H\}). \label{rel:numerical-data}$$ It gives $c_*=0$ when $n_1=n_2=0$. The same rule applies on every smooth projective surface with the same data and $\chi(\mathcal O_X)=1$, whether or not the lines $T,H$ are effective; effectivity is needed only for realizing the formula as a fixed contribution.

For either surface setting, and any $p\geq0$ with $v>p+2$, sum the classes [rel:fiber-contribution] with the following multiplicities:* 1. *If $p_g=q=0$, sum over the effective ordered line pairs $T+H=D$ and nonnegative point lengths satisfying [eq:length], with $m_T,m_H\geq0$. Each fixed part has multiplier $1$.* 2. *In the auxiliary setting, $D=3K$. Sum over the ordered pairs $(3K,0),(0,3K)$ with multiplier $1$, and $(2K,K),(K,2K)$ with multiplier $-s$, with the admissible point lengths. Here $s>0$ is the canonical-divisor coefficient of [eq:canonical-cycle].* *All sums are finite. Writing $c$ for the same weighted sum of the coefficients chosen in Proposition 23, one obtains $$0=c[\Delta_X]+\Gamma \qquad\text{in }\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}^2(X\times X), \label{rel:chow-identity}$$ where $\Gamma$ is a sum of external products of total codimension two.
If $p_g=q=0$ and the coefficient $c$ in [rel:chow-identity] is nonzero, then $\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}_0(X)^0\otimes\mathbb Q=0$.

Suppose $1\leq k_0\leq8$. Blow up $$e=\max\{k_0-5,0\}$$ distinct points of $X_0$, and call the resulting surface $X$. There are choices of $L_1,L_2,D,n,p$ on $X$ for which Theorem 24 gives a relation with $c>0$. Consequently the degree map on $\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}_0(X_0)_{\mathbb Q}$ is an isomorphism.
If $\Lambda$ is odd, there is a line bundle $h_0$ on $X_0$ with $$h_0^2=-1,\qquad K_0h_0=1.$$ If $\Lambda$ is even, then $k_0=8$ and there is a line bundle $h_0$ with $$h_0^2=0,\qquad K_0h_0=2.$$
Let $P$ be an effective line bundle on $X$ such that $m_P\geq0$ and $\alpha P\ne0$. Then $KP>k$.
The actual line bundles $$H=K+h',\qquad T=(d-1)K-h'$$ are effective and satisfy [nr:survivors], with $\alpha H\ne0$.

Let $X$ be a smooth minimal projective complex surface of general type with $p_g(X)=q(X)=0$ and $K_X^2=9$. Take $$\label{r1:data} L_1=L_2=0,\qquad D=3K_X,\qquad n=20,\qquad p=7.$$ The coefficient $c$ in the Chow relation of Theorem 24 is strictly positive.
For the data [r1:data], with numerical inputs $K^2=9$ and $\int c_2=3$, the two-order middle coefficient is $$c_{\mathrm{mid}}=12.$$

coverage.checked_domain: All k in {1,2,3,4,5}; exhaustive integer pairs satisfying the numerical hypotheses, with 0<=r<=d*k and 0<=s<=d*d*k. Boundary invalid inputs k=0,6 are rejected. No claim of effectivity or geometric existence is checked.
coverage.oracle_basis: Exact rational enumeration compared with independent integer constraints, exact witness rechecking and complete rectangular integer enumeration. Solver model enumeration is capped at 200 models and a solver timeout yields failure, never acceptance.
